title: The fuel-additive decoder round trip for first-order terms
statement: FO.Term.decodeAux, given at least FO.Term.size t units of fuel, returns t from FO.Term.code t. Stated additively -- for every t and every f, decodeAux (Nat.add f (size t)) (code t) = t -- so the theorem covers every sufficient fuel at once rather than one distinguished amount, and the corollary FO.Term.decode_code_at_size is the case f = Nat.zero. Together with F:fo-term-code-injective this makes FO.Term.code a genuine numbering: injective, and inverted by a total computable function of the code.

formal.statement: theorem FO.Term.decode_code : ((x0 : FO.Term) -> ((x1 : AxNat) -> Eq.{1} FO.Term (FO.Term.decodeAux (AxNat.add x1 (FO.Term.size x0)) (FO.Term.code x0)) x0))

evidence.supports: FO.Term.decode_code is admitted by the trusted kernel gate with the type recorded in formal.statement and rests on no axiom. It is one FO.Term.rec at the motive 'forall f, decodeAux (add f (size t)) (code t) = t', so the recursor's arity fixes all four constructor cases and a skipped case is not possible.
evidence.notes: Declared in crates/axeyum-lean-kernel/src/fo_roundtrip.rs by declare_decode_code, the same builder that produces FO.Formula.decode_code; the two differ only in the constructor table they are handed. The checker fails on absence.

evidence.supports: The theorem's declared type is rendered with Kernel::render_lean and compared against a literal in the test module, so a silently weakened statement (a dropped binder, a different decoder, the fuel on the other side of the Nat.add) fails the suite rather than passing unnoticed.

prior_art.what: arithmetization of syntax: a numbering of formulas whose decoding and substitution are primitive-recursive, and the diagonal identity that the code of a formula with its own numeral substituted is a computable function of the formula's code
prior_art.where: Goedel, 'Ueber formal unentscheidbare Saetze der Principia Mathematica und verwandter Systeme I', Monatshefte fuer Mathematik und Physik 38 (1931)
prior_art.attribution: standard textbook attribution; this lane did not consult the primary source

notes:
THE FUEL IS ON THE LEFT OF THE Nat.add AND THAT IS LOAD-BEARING. Nat.add recurses on its RIGHT argument in this prelude, so Nat.add f (Nat.succ x) iota-reduces to Nat.succ (Nat.add f x) and the decoder's step body appears at fuel Nat.add F (size child) -- LITERALLY the induction hypothesis's fuel, not merely a bound on it. Mutation RUN: rewriting the statement as Nat.add (size t) f makes the kernel reject the theorem with TypeMismatch and kills all twelve of the module's tests.

WHAT THIS IS NOT. It is not decode (code p) = p for the SELF-fuelled wrapper decode n := decodeAux n n. That would need Nat.le (size p) (code p), and that statement is FALSE: FO.Formula.code FO.Formula.bot and FO.Term.code (FO.Term.var 0) are both Nat.zero while both sizes are 1, pinned by Kernel::def_eq in fo_roundtrip/tests.rs::size_is_not_bounded_by_the_code. The self-fuelled wrappers are still believed correct -- the decoder spends one unit of fuel per constructor while FO.Code.pair a b is strictly larger than b -- but the route is a strong induction on the code with Nat.lt (FO.Code.snd n) n, which needs monotonicity of FO.Code.tri and a well-founded Nat recursion nobody has built. See F:fo-formula-decoder, which stays open for exactly that statement.

EACH MINOR COSTS ONE TRANSPORT ALONG FO.Code.fst_pair, because FO.Code.fst (FO.Code.pair 2 x) is NOT definitionally 2 -- FO.Code.fst unfolds to Nat.Pair.fst (unpair ...) and unpair of a symbolic code is a stuck Nat.rec. After the transport the tag tree's scrutinee is a literal numeral, the tree iota-reduces to its arm, and the arm's payload projections are rewritten one at a time along FO.Code.fst_pair / FO.Code.snd_pair.
